text:
John Carlson spent more than 1,100 games in Washington, won the Cup there in 2018, made a brief stop in Anaheim, and is now quarterbacking a Lightning team that's winning. He reached 800 career points with a career-best five-point night in Buffalo on Nov. 11, one goal and four assists in the rout, and followed it with another assist against Columbus. He's 36.

Tampa is controlling play with him on the ice: 60.1% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), more than six points better than when he sits. He has 16 points in 19 games, 11 in his last ten.

Some of it will settle. Six goals on 3.5 expected means he's shooting 14% against 9% last season, and his point rate sits above our talent range. Evolving-Hockey had him 17th among 215 defensemen last season, though, so the playmaking is real. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking names the weak spot: only 31% of his exits keep possession. Watch how he handles a heavy forecheck.
headline: Carlson hits 800, and fits in Tampa
